defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: Line 17: expanduser(f"~/{name}") prepends ~/ to NETRC value, so absolute paths resolve under $HOME (wrong file)
Line 12: NETRC="" yields ("",), resolves to home dir, netrc() fails; should fall back to NETRC_FILES
Test only covers relative NETRC name; no absolute-path test
Pre-existing: no test for raise_errors=True re-raise path
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` always prepends `~/` to the value of the `NETRC` variable, so an absolute path like `NETRC="/etc/custom.netrc"` becomes `~/etc/custom.netrc`, which `expanduser` resolves to `$HOME/etc/custom.netrc` — the wrong file entirely.
votes.justification: The review's first finding names the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth. It says an absolute NETRC path is wrongly resolved under the home directory, and that `~/` should only be prepended for bare filenames. That matches the known defect.
